record.paper_title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
record.original_question: Can the exact-sequence constructions and commuting diagrams obtained from M-decompositions and mixed-method spaces be rewritten in terms of the spaces of the corresponding HDG methods, in a way that yields exact sequences for discontinuous Galerkin methods?

evidence.quote: Exact sequences for DG methods. In the 2017 paper [ 29 ], a systematic way of constructing exact sequences, see [ 2 ], was presented which was based on the work on M-decompositions [ 27 , 28 , 55 ]. In the last part of the sequences, the spaces of a mixed method are used. Since, mixed methods can be recast as HDG methods, the corresponding commuting diagrams could be rewritten in terms of the spaces for the HDG method potentially giving rise to exact sequences for DG methods.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider second-order elliptic problems discretized by hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods on a conforming mesh $\mathcal{T}_h$ of a polyhedral domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$. For each element $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$, let $V(K) \times W(K)$ denote the local HDG approximation spaces for the flux and the scalar variable, and let $M(\partial K)$ denote the trace space on $\partial K$. Recall that an M-decomposition of $V(K) \times W(K)$ with respect to $M(\partial K)$ is an $L^2$-orthogonal decomposition
$$V(K)\times W(K) = \widetilde V(K)\times \widetilde W(K) \;\oplus\; V^{M}(K)\times W^{M}(K),$$
that allows one to identify the trace space $M(\partial K)$ with a quotient determined by $V^{M}(K)\times W^{M}(K)$, and which is the framework underlying systematic constructions of superconvergent mixed and HDG methods. Recall further that a finite element exact sequence (commuting de Rham-type diagram) for the corresponding mixed method takes the form
$$ \mathbb{R} \hookrightarrow \Lambda^0_h \xrightarrow{\nabla} \Lambda^1_h \xrightarrow{\nabla\times} \Lambda^2_h \xrightarrow{\nabla\cdot} \Lambda^3_h \to 0,$$
where the last spaces $\Lambda^{d-1}_h, \Lambda^d_h$ are the flux/scalar spaces of a mixed method that admits an M-decomposition, together with $L^2$-projection-type interpolants making the diagram commute.

Problem. Since every such mixed method can be reformulated as an HDG method, its global flux/scalar spaces are characterized by the local HDG spaces $V(K)$, $W(K)$ and the trace space $M(\partial K)$. Determine whether the exact-sequence constructions and commuting diagrams arising from M-decompositions can be rewritten purely in terms of the HDG spaces $\{V(K), W(K), M(\partial K)\}_{K\in\mathcal{T}_h}$ (together with appropriate trace operators and projections) in such a way that one obtains a finite element exact sequence with commuting interpolants whose terminal spaces are HDG spaces, thereby yielding exact sequences for discontinuous Galerkin methods. Explicitly construct such sequences, or show that no such reformulation can produce an exact sequence in the DG setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open direction within the literature on HDG methods and M-decompositions. The 2017 work on systematic construction of exact sequences via M-decompositions covers the mixed-method setting, and subsequent surveys describe rewriting these in HDG language as a potential route to DG exact sequences, but no published work appears to have carried out this construction or proved its impossibility. No solution was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing exact sequences for DG methods via M-decompositions as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The reformulation of M-decomposition exact sequences in HDG terms is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: An Introduction to the Theory of M-Decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces M-decompositions for systematic construction of superconvergent HDG/mixed methods and exact sequences in the mixed setting.
status_evidence.claim: Existing M-decomposition framework yields exact sequences for mixed methods, not yet recast for DG/HDG spaces.

status_evidence.title: Devising superconvergent HDG methods with symmetric approximate stresses for linear elasticity by M-decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: Develops HDG methods using M-decompositions; does not establish DG exact sequences.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works use M-decompositions for HDG construction without producing DG exact sequences.
